branch.new_demand: Generalize the verification with parameters into a proof for every line.
branch.builds_on: FORWARD 1 verifies for any center; FORWARD 2 proves the property for every line algebraically.

questions.skill: Prove algebraically that a dilation maps a line to a parallel line
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Prove that the dilation about the origin with scale factor k (k > 0, k ≠ 1) maps the line y = mx + b to the line y = mx + kb.
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that the dilation about the origin with scale factor k (k > 0, k ≠ 1) maps the line y = mx + b to the line y = mx + kb.
questions.correct_answer: The image of (x, mx + b) is (kx, kmx + kb), which satisfies y = mx + kb.
questions.required_method: Take any point (x, mx + b) on the line, find its image, and show the image satisfies y = mx + kb (and every point of that line is an image).
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: image (X, Y) = (kx, k(mx + b)); Y = m(kx) + kb = mX + kb; conversely (X, mX + kb) is the image of (X/k, mX/k + b). Conclusion: same slope m, so parallel when b ≠ 0, the same line when b = 0. Invalid: checking only two points of one example.
